Soojin —

We do have an informal threshold where vendors under $5k/month can be onboarded without a formal PO if they provide:
- Completed W9
- ACH or invoice remit details
- Bank validation (or Stripe/Fin platform confirmation)

For Procurely: their W9 is good. Ask them for ACH remit + vendor tax classification (LLC/C-Corp). We also prefer a short addendum (DocuSign) stating Redwood reserves the right to require PO after the 90-day window. I can route payment once we get ACH + vendor code.

Ben
Finance — Payments

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for sending the W9 and SOW. We've reviewed internally and can offer a temporary exception to our PO requirement under the following conditions:

1) Exception window: 90 days from the date the DocuSign addendum is signed. After 90 days, Redwood reserves the right to require a PO.
2) Threshold: invoices under USD 5,000/month may use the no-PO path for the pilot.
3) Required items before first invoice: signed DocuSign addendum (link below), completed vendor security questionnaire, and ACH or remit instructions.
4) Data handling: confirm pilot will not include PHI/PCI and retain logs for no more than 90 days.

DocuSign addendum: https://na1.docusign.net/DocuSign/guest/signing.aspx?env=na1&doc=ABC123
Vendor security questionnaire: https://docs.redwood.ai/vendor-questionnaire/procurely

Attachments: vendor_onboarding_packet.pdf (contains the addendum summary and steps). Once you return the signed addendum and the completed questionnaire + ACH remit, Ben will route the first payment on Net 30 terms. We'll do a policy review at day 60 and confirm continue/convert to PO path by day 90.

If anything is unclear, we can set a quick 20-minute sync. Looking forward to getting Procurely live.

Best,
Soojin Lee
